ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, if $AB$ and $AC$ are respectively one side of an inscribed equilateral triangle and one side of an inscribed square of circle $O$, and if $BC$ is one side of an inscribed regular $n$-sided polygon of circle $O$, then what is the value of $n$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw lines OA, OC, and OB. \\
Since AB and AC are respectively one side of a regular triangle and a regular square inscribed in circle O, \\
therefore, $\angle$AOC = $360^\circ \div 4 = 90^\circ$, $\angle$AOB = $360^\circ \div 3 = 120^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle$BOC = $\angle$AOB - $\angle$AOC = $120^\circ - 90^\circ = 30^\circ$, \\
therefore, n = $360^\circ \div 30^\circ = \boxed{12}$, \\
therefore, BC is definitely one side of a regular dodecagon inscribed in circle O.

AC is one side of a square inscribed in circle O, so the central angle ∠AOC corresponding to chord AC = 360°/4 = 90°. According to the figure, B and C are on the same side of A, and C is located between the arc from A to B, therefore ∠BOC = ∠AOB - ∠AOC = 120° - 90° = 30°. If BC is one side of a regular n-gon inscribed in circle O, then the central angle corresponding to it is 360°/n, so 360°/n = 30°, solving gives n = 12.
